summary: The interface shape is close to design doc 07 SS1 and the M1 subset (no putIfMatch, no multipart) is the right cut. Four interface-level problems: LIST requests are uncountable and ungovernable at the decorator seam that M1.3/M1.3b depend on; the conformance suite never exercises putIfAbsent concurrently, so the one property ADR-0002 rests on is unpinned; MemoryBinStore.list silently returns nothing when startAfter sorts before prefix; and Body.length is decorative -- no backend reads it and no test constrains it. Plus two contract gaps: past-EOF/zero-length ranges (named in design doc SS3) untested and divergent, and two record components from the design doc dropped without an ADR.

findings.title: The conformance suite never runs putIfAbsent concurrently -- the single property ADR-0002 rests on
findings.failure_scenario: putIfAbsentWritesOnlyWhenTheKeyIsFree is strictly sequential. Replace MemoryBinStore.java:96 with `if (objects.containsKey(key)) return Optional.empty(); objects.put(key, new Entry(data, v)); return Optional.of(v);` -- a non-atomic get-then-put -- and the entire suite still passes green. That is a named surviving mutation on the exact guarantee ADR-0002 calls the coordination substrate and that design doc 07 SS3 lists as conformance bullet one ('putIfAbsent succeeds exactly once under N concurrent writers; all others observe exists'). The consequence is not theoretical: M1.2's LocalFsBinStore implements putIfAbsent via O_CREAT|O_EXCL and M1.4/M1.5 via If-None-Match; a backend that gets the race wrong ships with a green conformance run, two writers both observe absence, and the loser overwrites the winner's commit-log record with no error -- invariant I1 violated silently, which is data loss discovered only at replay. This is the harness's headline deliverable and it is the one case it does not cover. Fix: N threads (executor + CountDownLatch, no Thread.sleep per testing.md rule 15) racing putIfAbsent on one key; assert exactly one non-empty Optional, N-1 empties, and that get() returns the winner's body.

findings.title: list returns a lazily paged Stream, so LIST requests cannot be counted or refused at the SPI seam
findings.failure_scenario: The signature is `Stream<ObjectStat> list(prefix, startAfter)` with no maxKeys and no page abstraction, and paging is internal to the backend's spliterator. A decorator wrapping BinStore -- which is exactly what M1.3 CountingBinStore and M1.3b GoverningBinStore are -- observes ONE list() invocation no matter whether S3 issued 1 or 10,000 ListObjectsV2 requests. Concretely: a recovery walk over a prefix holding 10M keys is 10,000 billed LIST requests and the cost meter records 1, so cost.md R9 ('every store operation is counted and attributable') under-reports by four orders of magnitude and the assertion the standard says to write first, assertThat(stats.listRequests()).isZero(), can be satisfied by a run that issued thousands. Worse for R15/rule 12: the LIST hard ceiling (~1/s) is a *refusal*, and a governor cannot refuse page 500 of a stream it did not open without throwing UncheckedIOException out of a terminal operation -- which is the very thing BinStore.java:31 says the checked IOException exists to avoid. cost.md rule 12 is explicit that counting catches a regression in review and only refusing catches one in production, and names per-shard LIST polling at $21,600/hour as the runaway this guards. Design doc 07 SS1 does draw `Stream ... // lazily paged`, so this is a conflict between that sketch and the decorator seam the same document defines in SS5 -- but it is settled now or not at all, because it is a signature change once LocalFs/S3/GCS/Azure implement it. Either return an explicit page (`ListPage list(prefix, startAfter, int maxKeys)` with a nextStartAfter, one page == one request == one countable unit) or state in the javadoc how a decorator counts and bounds pages, and give the SPI a per-call key ceiling. As it stands the constraint is a comment, which is what question 3 asked.

findings.title: list returns an empty stream when startAfter sorts before prefix, instead of the prefix's keys
findings.failure_scenario: When startAfter != null the tailMap seeks from startAfter alone and ignores prefix; takeWhile then terminates at the FIRST key that does not match the prefix. So list("p/", "other/a") -- or, more likely to occur, list("p/", "") with an empty-string resume token from a checkpoint that has never advanced -- positions before "p/", hits a non-matching key immediately, and returns ZERO objects while p/a, p/b, p/c exist. S3 and GCS ignore a start-after that is below the prefix and return the full prefix listing, so LocalFs/Memory and S3 will disagree the first time a caller passes one. Because R2 confines LIST to recovery and GC, the observable failure is recovery concluding 'nothing to recover' and silently skipping every segment under the prefix -- no exception, no log, unreplayed data. Fix: seek from max(prefix, startAfter), i.e. `objects.tailMap(startAfter.compareTo(prefix) > 0 ? startAfter : prefix, startAfter.compareTo(prefix) > 0 ? false : true)`, and add a conformance case pinning startAfter-below-prefix so every backend agrees.

findings.title: Body.length is never read by the only backend and never constrained by the suite, so the fake accepts writes S3 rejects
findings.failure_scenario: MemoryBinStore.readFully (MemoryBinStore.java:41) calls in.readAllBytes() and ignores body.length() entirely; no conformance test asserts any relationship between the declared length and the bytes stored. Delete the `length` component from the record and every test in this diff still passes -- a surviving mutation on a component the javadoc calls load-bearing ('stores need it up front for content-length'). The failure this hides: a writer that computes length from a stale count and supplies a stream of a different size passes every T0/T1 run against MemoryBinStore, then against S3 either sends Content-Length larger than the body (the SDK errors mid-request, or worse the object lands truncated) or smaller (the body is silently cut at Content-Length and the segment is corrupt on read). Since 'a mismatch is the caller's bug' is stated but unenforced, and the conformance suite is the only place backends are held to the same contract, add a case asserting that a Body whose stream yields more or fewer bytes than length is rejected -- or that stat().size() equals the declared length after a put -- and have MemoryBinStore enforce it so it is no more permissive than the backend it stands in for.

findings.title: Past-EOF and zero-length range behaviour is unspecified in the SPI and untested, and MemoryBinStore throws where S3 clamps
findings.failure_scenario: getRange's contract is one line ('Bytes [start, endIncl], streamed') and says nothing about a range extending past the object; MemoryBinStore throws IOException whenever endIncl >= data.length. S3, GCS and MinIO return 206 with the available bytes and only fail (416) when start is beyond the end. Design doc 07 SS3 names this explicitly as a conformance requirement -- 'Range reads: zero-length, past-EOF, and last-byte ranges behave identically everywhere' -- and SS2b lists past-EOF ranges as one of the things the MinIO fixture exists to exercise. The suite tests only the last-byte and interior cases, so the divergence lands undetected: code written and green against MemoryBinStore behaves differently the moment it runs on S3, and vice versa. It also bears on cost R7 -- 'one speculative range read, not footer-then-index' -- because a speculative read is by construction one that may over-read, and a backend that hard-fails on over-read forces callers into stat-then-range, doubling requests per segment for no reason. Pick the semantics (clamp, matching every real backend), state them on the interface, and pin them in the suite for past-EOF, start-beyond-EOF and zero-length.

findings.title: Two record components specified by design doc 07 SS1 are dropped, and re-adding either is the signature change the task says to avoid
findings.failure_scenario: The design doc specifies `Capabilities(conditionalWrites, batchDelete, maxKeyBytes, minPartSize, CostTable costs)` and `ObjectStat(key, size, version, long lastModifiedMillis)`. The diff drops CostTable with no mention anywhere, and lastModifiedMillis with a javadoc note but no ADR. CostTable is not incidental: the doc's one-line takeaway is that the two things added beyond AutoMQ's SPI are conditional writes and a cost meter, and M1.3 (CountingBinStore + cost-assertion fixture) is the very next task -- it will need per-request-class pricing and will have to put it back. Adding a component to a record changes its canonical constructor, so every `new ObjectStat(...)` in every backend and every `new Capabilities(...)` breaks at that point; by M1.3/M1.4 that is LocalFs, S3 and the fixtures. This is precisely the 'genuinely ADDITIONS later rather than signature changes' property the task set as the bar, and it holds for putIfMatch/multipart (new methods) but not for these two. Either carry the components now, or record the narrowing as an ADR per the adr skill's 'when changing the store SPI' trigger so M1.3 is not surprised. (ObjectStat's timestamp exclusion is well argued in the javadoc and may well be right -- what is missing is that the argument lives where a future reader looks, and that dropping it was a decision rather than an omission.)
